golang-testing/SKILL.md.old:
Name the test file after the source file it tests, not after the function or method under test. Go's convention is one test file per source file (`foo.go` -> `foo_test.go`), because tools (`go test`, coverage reports, IDE "jump to test" navigation, `gotests`) and reviewers all resolve tests by source file, not by symbol. A source file usually declares several functions/methods; splitting its tests by symbol name scatters them across many files and breaks that file-to-file mapping.

```
// ✓ Good — one test file per source file
helloworld.go       -> helloworld_test.go   // contains TestHelloWorld, TestAbcd, TestXyz, ...

// ✗ Bad — test file named after the function/method instead of the source file
helloworld.go       -> abcd_test.go         // wrong: should be helloworld_test.go
```

Exception: very large source files MAY be split into multiple `_test.go` files by concern (e.g. `foo_test.go` + `foo_edgecases_test.go`), but each split file's name MUST still be derived from the source file name, never from an individual function name. Prefer keeping a single `_test.go` file per source file even when it grows large — splitting adds navigation overhead and is rarely worth it; reach for the exception only when a single file becomes genuinely unwieldy to browse or review.

Within a test file, order test functions to match the order their tested functions/methods appear in the source file. A reader (human or agent) scrolling `foo.go` alongside `foo_test.go` can then find the matching test by position instead of searching; drift between the two orderings compounds every time either file grows.
golang-testing/SKILL.md.new:
Use descriptive `*_test.go` names that fit the package and existing repository conventions. `foo_test.go`, `user_validation_test.go` and `authorization_test.go` can all be appropriate. Choose grouping and test order for readability and behavior coverage; do not rename files or reorder tests solely to match production source files.

Integration tests need a documented way to run independently when they require external services or expensive setup. Reuse the project's existing build tags, package boundaries, flags, environment selection or CI commands; adding `//go:build integration` is one option, not a universal requirement.

golang-project-layout/evals/evals.json.new: Flags request parsing, database queries and response formatting as responsibilities that do not belong in the entry point

golang-project-layout/evals/evals.json.old: Recommends putting main.go inside cmd/{name}/ not at root or in src/
golang-project-layout/evals/evals.json.new: Recommends moving main.go out of src/; the module root and cmd/{name}/ are both valid

golang-project-layout/evals/evals.json.old: Puts the shared logging library in pkg/ (useful to external consumers)
golang-project-layout/evals/evals.json.new: Puts the shared logging library in an importable package (module root or pkg/); pkg/ is optional

golang-project-layout/evals/evals.json.old: Service/business logic goes in internal/ by default
golang-project-layout/evals/evals.json.new: Keeps service/business packages out of pkg/ and uses internal/ where the import restriction is actually useful

golang-project-layout/evals/evals.json.old: Business logic is in internal/, not duplicated across cmd/ directories
golang-project-layout/evals/evals.json.new: Shared logic lives in a common package rather than being duplicated across cmd/ directories

golang-testing/evals/evals.json.old: Uses `//go:build integration` build tag (at the file level, before the package declaration)
golang-testing/evals/evals.json.new: Selects integration tests independently using the project's existing mechanism (build tag, separate package, flag, environment configuration or dedicated command)

golang-testing/evals/evals.json.old: Explains why build tags are preferred: tests using testing.Short() still compile and attempt connections when running without -short, whereas build-tagged files are completely excluded from compilation
golang-testing/evals/evals.json.new: Explains that the selection mechanism must gate expensive setup: a build tag removes the file from compilation, while testing.Short() still compiles and can attempt connections without -short

golang-testing/evals/evals.json.old: Includes the command to run integration tests: go test -tags=integration ./...
golang-testing/evals/evals.json.new: Shows how to run the integration tests with the selected mechanism
Makes the integration tests selectable through the project's chosen mechanism (for example a build tag)

golang-project-layout/evals/evals.json.name: local-existing-service-lookup
golang-project-layout/evals/evals.json.description: 本地用例：在已有服务里加查询路径时必须复用现有布局与装配
golang-project-layout/evals/evals.json.prompt: This checkout is an existing Go service. We need to add an endpoint that returns all orders for one user. Show how you would wire it through the code that is already here, and list the files you would add or change.
golang-project-layout/evals/evals.json.trap: Tempts scaffolding a service/repository/domain layer or a pkg/ wrapper for a query that belongs next to the existing store methods, or replacing explicit constructors with a DI framework

assertions.text: Reads the existing entry point, store package or README before proposing the change
Keeps the existing package layout: no new cmd/, service/, repository/ or domain/ directories and no pkg/ wrapper
Adds the query to the existing store type and reuses the existing constructor wiring; no DI framework, ORM or extra abstraction layer

golang-testing/evals/evals.json.name: local-reuse-existing-integration-selection
golang-testing/evals/evals.json.description: 本地用例：新增集成测试必须沿用项目既有的选中机制
golang-testing/evals/evals.json.prompt: This checkout is an existing Go service with tests. We are adding a ListByUserID query to the order store and need integration tests for it. Check how this project runs its tests today, then tell me what you would add and which commands to run.
golang-testing/evals/evals.json.trap: Tempts forcing //go:build integration onto a project that already selects integration tests through an environment variable, or splitting the suite into new test packages

assertions.text: Reads the existing test files or README before recommending how to add integration tests
Keeps the project's env-var integration-test selection and does not migrate the suite to build tags
Keeps the existing test layout: no separate tests/ directory and no new test packages for the suite
